small_guidance:
- Add wider autotune configs that exploit the 4-output reuse: BLOCK_SP=32/64 with BLOCK_OC=128/256 and BLOCK_K=64/128, num_warps=8, num_stages=2-4 — the inner loop does 4 tl.dot per K tile so larger BLOCK_OC amortizes weight loads.
- Try swapping the program grid order to (pid_n, pid_oc, pid_sp) or use `tl.swizzle2d` on (pid_sp, pid_oc) to improve L2 reuse of the weight tile across spatial tiles within the same batch.
- Hoist the `b_val - SUB1` and constant `1/(POOL*POOL)` scaling outside the tanh, and combine the four accumulators into a single (BLOCK_OC, 4, BLOCK_SP) tensor so the epilogue is one tanh call on a single block (fewer exp instructions, better ILP).
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM with channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous in memory; this turns the 4 strided gather loads into 4 vector loads with stride IC and dramatically improves load efficiency on the 4090.
- Restructure to one program per (N, OC tile, pooled-spatial tile) emitting the pooled output directly via 4 dot products sharing the same weight tile — but materialize the 2x2 pool window as a single (BLOCK_SP*4) gather and use a single `tl.dot` of shape (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K) x (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SP*4), then reduce-by-4 in the epilogue. This halves the dot count and increases tensor-core utilization.
- Alternatively, persist weights in shared memory across N (persistent-kernel over batch): loop pid_n inside the kernel for a fixed (oc, sp) tile so the weight tile is loaded once per (oc, sp) and reused across all 128 batches — weight reuse is currently the dominant traffic.
